newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour has no plans to change top tax rate.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour has no plans to change top tax rate.

text.p: Britain's main opposition Labour Party has no plans for the time being to change the top rate of tax, which currently stands at 40 percent, party leader Tony Blair said on Wednesday. "We have no proposals to raise the top rate of tax. If that changes, then we will make those changes clear," he told BBC radio. Labour holds a healthy opinion poll lead in the run-up to the next election, whch must be held by May 1997.
There has been widespread speculation that Labour might impose a top tax rate of 50 percent for those people earning more than 100,000 pounds a year.

"If there are any changes on tax on spending that we want to make...we will disclose them well in advance of the general election," Blair said a day after Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke had revealed his budget.
Asked whether Labour still planned to announce any such changes in January, Blair replied: "That is precisely correct."

He said Labour would not vote against a planned one point cut in the basic rate of tax to 23 percent on the grounds that people needed some relief from what he said were large tax rises imposed by the ruling Conservatives.
But he denied that this would leave his party facing a credibility gap with voters.
"We would have a credibility gap if we were saying that we can promise you all sorts of extra money but not say where it's coming from," he said.
"This idea that there's no difference between the two parties is simply not correct," he said.

Blair said a future government would be constrained by what he described as the errors the Conservatives had made. "Any government's going to be hemmed in by the mistakes...They're hemmed in by the problems on inflation, on interest rates, on public sector debt," he said.
